edges.mechanism: Possible potentiation of anticoagulation and bleeding; proposed antiplatelet and pharmacokinetic mechanisms. A controlled PK/PD study in healthy men found no INR or warfarin clearance change.
edges.evidence: Case report (phenprocoumon, INR 10 with epistaxis, probable causality); prospective warfarin cohort (ginger bleeding OR 3.20); crossover PK/PD study null; systematic reviews list ginger among bleeding-risk herbs; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Additive bleeding tendency theoretically possible; review notes food-herb interactions may also be relevant for DOACs.
edges.evidence: Evidence review without ginger-specific DOAC data; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Gingerols inhibit arachidonic-acid-dependent platelet aggregation in vitro; human platelet data equivocal (4 of 8 trials positive).
edges.evidence: Systematic review of platelet studies; bleeding review rates ginger evidence conflicting; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Both Zingiberaceae extracts and NSAIDs have been associated with heightened bleeding risk; no comparator trials of combined risk.
edges.evidence: Meta-analysis discussion; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Ginger potentiated the anti-platelet-aggregation effect of nifedipine (1 g ginger + 10 mg nifedipine); additive blood-pressure lowering also plausible.
edges.evidence: Small human platelet study in hypertensive patients and volunteers; BP MA

edges.mechanism: Ginger lowers fasting glucose and HbA1c in T2D; additive glucose lowering possible.
edges.evidence: MAs of RCTs (FBS -16.27 mg/dL, HbA1c -0.41%); heterogeneous; no direct interaction study

edges.mechanism: Additive glucose lowering possible given ginger's FBS/HbA1c reductions in T2D trials (many participants on background metformin).
edges.evidence: Inferred from MAs; no direct interaction study

edges.mechanism: Modest additive BP reduction (SBP about -5 mmHg).
edges.evidence: GRADE-low MA of 12 RCTs

edges.mechanism: Ginger constituents inhibit CYP3A4 and P-gp in vitro, which could raise tacrolimus exposure; a renal-transplant case found no trough change with 10 g/d for 4 days.
edges.evidence: Review, in-vitro data and single case report; very low certainty

edges.with: CYP3A4/P-gp substrates with narrow therapeutic index
edges.mechanism: In-vitro inhibition of CYP3A4, 2C9, 1A2, 2B6, P-gp and BCRP by ginger extract and constituents at concentrations potentially reached in the gut.
edges.evidence: In-vitro study plus kinase-inhibitor case report; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Reported pharmacokinetic herb-drug interaction with serious consequences, consistent with CYP3A4 inhibition.
edges.evidence: Single case report

edges.mechanism: Stacking bleeding-associated supplements; garlic strongly associated with surgical bleeding, ginger evidence conflicting.
edges.evidence: Narrative review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Turmeric is associated with bleeding in anticoagulated patients and, like ginger, is listed as a putative CYP3A4 inhibitor (tacrolimus).
edges.evidence: Reviews and case report (no tacrolimus change); very low certainty

edges.mechanism: In warfarin users both CoQ10 (OR 3.69) and ginger (OR 3.20) were independently associated with self-reported bleeding; use of more than one CAM was itself a risk factor.
edges.evidence: Prospective cohort (n=171); low certainty

edges.mechanism: Both listed among herbs increasing bleeding risk with warfarin; neither altered warfarin PK/PD in healthy men.
edges.evidence: Systematic review and crossover study; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Effective for nausea of pregnancy; cohorts show no excess malformations, one small confounded cohort had a borderline stillbirth signal; EU HMPC advises against use for lack of adequate data while NCCIH says it may be safe.
edges.evidence: MAs of RCTs, MoBa cohort (n=68,522), Korean cohort, regulator texts

edges.mechanism: Insufficient safety data; EU HMPC advises against use while breastfeeding.
edges.evidence: Regulator statements only

edges.mechanism: EU HMPC: not for children under 6 (motion sickness) or under 18 (other indications) due to lack of data.
edges.evidence: Regulator monograph

edges.mechanism: Equivocal antiplatelet activity; review advises stopping non-essential supplements 2 weeks before surgery.
edges.evidence: Narrative review and platelet SR

edges.mechanism: Not an assay artifact; ginger may truly raise INR in patients on vitamin K antagonists.
edges.evidence: Case report and evidence review
